sources.title: Abuja Area Mama, Nigerian transgender TikToker, found dead
sources.claim_summary: BBC News (9 August 2024): a 33-year-old transgender TikToker known as "Abuja Area Mama", with ~10,000 followers and a previously reported stabbing, was found beaten beside the Katampe-Mabushi Expressway in the capital hours after posting; police opened a murder investigation and the article notes that mass arrests and detentions of LGBTQ+ Nigerians are common, especially in northern states.

sources.title: Threats, Raids and Potlucks — The Dial
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page content was site navigation only at fetch time; the underlying feature (issue 25, LGBTQ rights in Nigeria) covers the threats-and-raids climate around the capital's queer scene alongside informal community organising (per country dossier).

Sahara Reporters (19 August 2026): the UK foreign office's travel advisory warns LGBT+ travellers of arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation in Nigeria - same-sex conduct carries up to 14 years federally, and some northern states' Sharia law prescribes the death penalty for it; the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act criminalises attending, organising or promoting same-sex weddings and registering or publicly promoting gay groups; the advisory also warns that mobile networks can be suspended and curfews imposed with little notice.
